question: What type of compound is formed when one hydrogen atom in ammonia is substituted by an alkyl or aromatic group?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary amine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary Amine:** 

 
 
• Primary amines are formed when **one hydrogen atom** in **ammonia** is substituted by an **alkyl or aromatic group**.
 
• Some **examples** of primary alkyl amines include **amino acids** and **methylamine** while primary aromatic amines include **aniline**.
 
 
 
• **Secondary** **Amine:**
 
 
• Secondary amines are those amines that have **two organic substituents** either **alkyl** or **aryl ones or both**. They are bound to the nitrogen together with one hydrogen. A common example is **dimethylamine**. Likewise, diphenylamine is an example of an **aromatic amine**.
 
• 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d00360317628e577b6e85affad664506664b0c3369a52f9f3db4e1603f02c5c.png] 

 
Methyl isocyanide can be reduced to secondary amine in the presence of Lithium aluminum hydride (LiAIH4)

 
CH3NC → CH3NHCH3 ( in the presence of Lithium aluminum hydride)

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Carboxylic acid

 
 
• It is an organic compound containing a carboxyl functional group. They occur widely in nature and are produced synthetically. 
 
• The general formula of a carboxylic acid is R-COOH, where COOH refers to the carboxyl group and R refers to the rest of the molecule to which this carboxyl group is attached.
 
 
• In this case, there is a carbon that shares a double bond with an oxygen atom and a single bond with a hydroxyl group.
 
 
 
• The first four carboxylic acids derived from alkanes are - 
 
 
• Methanoic acid (Formic acid)
 
 
• 1 carbon
 
• HCOOH
 
 
 
• Ethanoic acid (Acetic acid or vinegar)
 
 
• 2 carbon
 
• CH3COOH
 
 
 
• Propanoic acid
 
 
• 3 carbon
 
• C2H5COOH
 
 
 
• Butanoic acid
 
 
• 4 carbon
 
• C3H7COOH
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Ketone Body**:
 
 
• Ketone bodies are contained by the ketone group. 
 
• This **water-soluble compound** is produced in the **liver** during **caloric restrictions**.
 
• Ketone bodies act as an **energy source** in the **absence of glucose**.
 
• Ketone body when present in the liver is called **ketogenesis**.
